Nick, that is handled by the ‘effort’ variable.  If a point is surveyed x times, then the survey effort is x.  When some points are surveyed more times than others, it must be assumed that the number of times a point is surveyed is independent of animal density, so normally, it is good practice to keep the number of visits constant, at least within a stratum.

 

Steve Buckland

Subject: [distance-sampling] How to set up multipliers for point transect data?

 

Hi everyone,

I have point transect data that I'm importing into Distance and I can't figure out how to assign unique multipliers to my dataset to account for the fact that individual points were surveyed a different number of times (i.e., not all points were surveyed the same number of times). I've figured out how to do a "global" multiplier that would apply one multiplier to my data, but that's not quite what I want. And when I go into the Model Definition Properties for the Default Model Definition, under the Multipliers tab, "Global" is the only option under "Layer type containing multiplier." I have a column in my dataset that contains the multiplier for each point, so I just need a way to tell Distance to look in that location. Thanks in advance for the help.

Regards,
Nick Peterson
